# Porting a LightGBM, XGBoost, or CatBoost configuration

**Generated by `python3 tools/port_report.py --write`. Do not edit by
hand.** Every table below comes out of `mojotrees.port`, through the same
`PortReport.render()` that prints in a console, so this page and that call
cannot disagree.

    from mojotrees import port

    report = port(my_params, source="lightgbm")
    print(report)                        # the tables below, for your dict
    model = MojoTreesRegressor(**report.params)

`port()` sorts every key you passed into four categories.

| category | what it means |
|---|---|
| `honored` | ours under the same name, and the value is used as you gave it |
| `aliased_to` | a vendor spelling of one of our canonical names; the report gives both names |
| `defaulted_differently` | we accept it, you did not name it, and our default is not that vendor's, so your model will differ from theirs unless you set it |
| `refused` | we do not implement it, with the reason this repository already states for it |

A fifth list, `unsourced`, is not a category. It is every fact the report
wanted and could not read. An answer that cannot be sourced appears there
as an absence rather than being guessed at, which is why some rows below
say `unknown` instead of a number.

Where the facts come from is in the module docstring of
`python/mojotrees/port.py`. In short, the alias table is derived from the
`_resolve_alias` call sites that `tools/api_snapshot.py` also reads,
LightGBM's stock defaults and our declared departures from them come from
`tools/check_parity.py`, XGBoost's and CatBoost's resolved defaults come
from the tables in `bench/real_data/scenarios.py` that record the library
call each was read back from, and refusal reasons come from section 7 of
`docs/LIGHTGBM_PARITY.md`.

Two notes on reading the pages below.

- `defaulted_differently` is computed for a caller who set **nothing**, and
  then again for the worked example. A parameter you name yourself leaves
  that list, because you have already decided it.
- `declared` in that table says whether the departure is registered in
  `STOCK_DIVERGENCES` in `tools/check_parity.py` with a reason and an exit
  condition. A `yes` is an argument on the page. A `no` means only that this
  repository records the vendor's value and not a reason for the gap.

in `_Base`, which is the same derivation that produces the
`parameter_aliases` block of `compatibility/api_snapshot.json`. `we call it`

computes it rather than spelling it out.

## lightgbm

### If you set nothing

What changes for a caller who ports a lightgbm script and names no hyperparameter at all.

an empty dict, source=lightgbm

0 honored, 0 aliased, 2 defaulted differently, 0 refused, 0 unsourced.

**defaulted_differently.** You did not name these and our default is not lightgbm's, so your model will differ from lightgbm's unless you set them.

| parameter     | their name    | their default | our default | declared | reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|-------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| enable_bundle | enable_bundle | True          | False       | yes      | exclusive feature bundling changes the feature space before binning, and mojotrees's EFB is not applied by every trainer yet (the ranking trainer refuses an active bundling switch by name). Off by default until it is; see the enable_bundle row of docs/LIGHTGBM_PARITY.md                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| reg_lambda    | lambda_l2     | 0.0           | 1.0         | yes      | the one default in this library with recorded accuracy damage on THREE separate scenarios, and the only reason it was 0.0 is that LightGBM's is 0.0, which is a mirror and not a measurement. docs/design/ACCURACY_GAP.md section 3.4 has the artifacts: -1.6 percent of excess error on dense_regression (matched bin digest, two-point, estimate), 0.75x average precision on imbalanced_binary and 3.31x worse multiclass logloss (both measured, and both cost us more than they cost LightGBM) ... |

**notes.**

- Every LightGBM stock default not listed above is asserted equal to ours by tools/check_parity.py, on the Mojo and the Python surface both, so an undeclared difference fails CI rather than reaching this report.

**fact sources.**

| fact                                 | read from                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| accepted parameters and our defaults | python/mojotrees/sklearn.py                                                                                |
| canonical spellings                  | docs/PARAMETER_NAMING.md, the OURS column                                                                  |
| lightgbm stock defaults              | tools/check_parity.py LIGHTGBM_STOCK, read from microsoft/LightGBM include/LightGBM/config.h at tag v4.7.0 |
| refusal reasons                      | docs/LIGHTGBM_PARITY.md, section 7                                                                         |
| vendor alias table                   | python/mojotrees/sklearn.py, the _Base._resolve_alias call sites                                           |

### A worked example

```python
port({'num_leaves': 63, 'learning_rate': 0.05, 'num_iterations': 500, 'min_sum_hessian_in_leaf': 0.01, 'feature_pre_filter': True, 'forcedsplits_filename': 'splits.json', 'label': 'y'},
     source='lightgbm')
```

that dict, source=lightgbm

2 honored, 2 aliased, 2 defaulted differently, 3 refused, 0 unsourced.

**honored.** Ours under the same name, used as given.

| parameter     | value | owner  | note |
|---------------|-------|--------|------|
| num_leaves    | 63    | shared |      |
| learning_rate | 0.05  | shared |      |

**aliased_to.** A vendor spelling of one of our names. The value is used as given, under the canonical name. `we call it` is the spelling to type; `on the wire` is the spelling the native layer is sent and the model file holds, and the two differ for eleven parameters.

| you passed              | we call it       | on the wire    | value | note |
|-------------------------|------------------|----------------|-------|------|
| num_iterations          | n_estimators     | n_estimators   | 500   |      |
| min_sum_hessian_in_leaf | min_child_weight | min_child_hess | 0.01  |      |

**defaulted_differently.** You did not name these and our default is not lightgbm's, so your model will differ from lightgbm's unless you set them.

| parameter     | their name    | their default | our default | declared | reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|-------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| enable_bundle | enable_bundle | True          | False       | yes      | exclusive feature bundling changes the feature space before binning, and mojotrees's EFB is not applied by every trainer yet (the ranking trainer refuses an active bundling switch by name). Off by default until it is; see the enable_bundle row of docs/LIGHTGBM_PARITY.md                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| reg_lambda    | lambda_l2     | 0.0           | 1.0         | yes      | the one default in this library with recorded accuracy damage on THREE separate scenarios, and the only reason it was 0.0 is that LightGBM's is 0.0, which is a mirror and not a measurement. docs/design/ACCURACY_GAP.md section 3.4 has the artifacts: -1.6 percent of excess error on dense_regression (matched bin digest, two-point, estimate), 0.75x average precision on imbalanced_binary and 3.31x worse multiclass logloss (both measured, and both cost us more than they cost LightGBM) ... |

**refused.** We do not implement these, and why.

| parameter             | value         | status             | reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | cited from                                |
|-----------------------|---------------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| feature_pre_filter    | True          | partial            | **Implemented, and reachable from the Mojo API only.** LightGBM's `true` is a Dataset construction step: `BinMapper::FindBin` marks a feature trivial when `NeedFilter(cnt_in_bin, total_sample_cnt, min_split_data, bin_type)` finds no prefix of its bins leaving at least `min_split_data` rows on both sides, and ... | docs/LIGHTGBM_PARITY.md section 7         |
| forcedsplits_filename | 'splits.json' | unsupported        | File-based configuration surface. `src/mojotrees/tree_parameters_extra.mojo` can parse the file's contents into a validated forced-split tree, but reading a file is not something mojotrees does                                                                                                                         | docs/LIGHTGBM_PARITY.md section 7         |
| label                 | 'y'           | belongs to Dataset | 'label' describes the data, not the training run; pass it as Dataset(label=...)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | python/mojotrees/basic.py _DATASET_PARAMS |

**notes.**

- Every LightGBM stock default not listed above is asserted equal to ours by tools/check_parity.py, on the Mojo and the Python surface both, so an undeclared difference fails CI rather than reaching this report.

Cross-checked against XGBRegressor().get_params(), which in 3.4.0 returns None for every tree parameter and is therefore not a source. ### A worked example

```python
port({'eta': 0.05, 'max_depth': 8, 'reg_lambda': 2.0, 'colsample_bytree': 0.8, 'alpha': 1.0, 'tree_method': 'hist'},
     source='xgboost')
```

### A worked example

```python
port({'iterations': 500, 'depth': 8, 'l2_leaf_reg': 3.0, 'one_hot_max_size': 10, 'bootstrap_type': 'MVS', 'nan_mode': 'Min'},
     source='catboost')
```

that dict, source=catboost

1 honored, 4 aliased, 5 defaulted differently, 1 refused, 16 unsourced.

**honored.** Ours under the same name, used as given.

| parameter      | value | owner  | note |
|----------------|-------|--------|------|
| bootstrap_type | 'MVS' | shared |      |

**aliased_to.** A vendor spelling of one of our names. The value is used as given, under the canonical name. `we call it` is the spelling to type; `on the wire` is the spelling the native layer is sent and the model file holds, and the two differ for eleven parameters.

| you passed       | we call it        | on the wire       | value | note |
|------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------|------|
| iterations       | n_estimators      | n_estimators      | 500   |      |
| depth            | max_depth         | max_depth         | 8     |      |
| l2_leaf_reg      | reg_lambda        | lambda_l2         | 3.0   |      |
| one_hot_max_size | max_cat_to_onehot | max_cat_to_onehot | 10    |      |

**defaulted_differently.** You did not name these and our default is not catboost's, so your model will differ from catboost's unless you set them.

| parameter         | their name       | their default   | our default | declared | reason                                                                                                   |
|-------------------|------------------|-----------------|-------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| max_bin           | border_count     | 254             | 255         | no       | no per-parameter reason for this difference is recorded in this repository; only catboost's own value is |
| grow_policy       | grow_policy      | 'SymmetricTree' | 'lossguide' | no       | no per-parameter reason for this difference is recorded in this repository; only catboost's own value is |
| max_leaves        | max_leaves       | 64              | 31          | no       | no per-parameter reason for this difference is recorded in this repository; only catboost's own value is |
| min_child_samples | min_data_in_leaf | 1               | 20          | no       | no per-parameter reason for this difference is recorded in this repository; only catboost's own value is |
| subsample         | subsample        | 0.8             | 1.0         | no       | no per-parameter reason for this difference is recorded in this repository; only catboost's own value is |
